summary: Remote WebSocket server drives PTY, filesystem, and self-upgrade on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs as a long-lived agent (bin `yeaft-agent`, `npm start`) that connects to a WebSocket server (default `ws://localhost:3456`, overridable via `SERVER_URL`) and treats server-sent messages as commands. `handleTerminalCreate` spawns a local PTY (bash/pwsh) via `pty.spawn`, and `handleTerminalInput` writes attacker-supplied `msg.data` directly into that PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), giving whoever controls the configured server an interactive shell on the installer's host. Additional handlers expose file read/write and git operations. An `upgrade_agent` message handler invokes `buildUpgradeInstallCommand("${pkgName}@latest")` and launches a detached `bash upgrade.sh` / `upgrade.bat` that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restarts the service (systemd/launchd/PM2), so the same remote server can force the host to fetch and execute an unpinned future version at any time. The default server is loopback and the URL is user-configurable, but the code path unconditionally treats the configured server as a fully trusted remote-control channel; a non-loopback `SERVER_URL`, a compromised or malicious server, or anyone reaching the loopback port grants full shell, filesystem, and self-update control over the installer's machine. `service/linux.js` also modifies `PATH` to prepend `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` when the agent is installed as a service.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
